documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Chief complaint: shortness of breath and leg swelling x 5 days
HPI:
62 yo F with HFrEF (EF 30% on echo 8 mo ago), HTN, T2DM, CKD stage 3, presents with progressive dyspnea.
Symptoms began about a week ago with exertional dyspnea climbing stairs, now dyspnea at rest.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Orthopnea worsened from 1 pillow to 3 pillows; wakes at night gasping 2 to 3 times.
Denies chest pain, fever, cough productive of sputum, hemoptysis.
Denies recent dietary indiscretion, though admits canned soup most evenings.
No syncope. No palpitations. No recent med changes other than diuretic titration.
Brought in by daughter after she noted pt could not walk to the bathroom without stopping.
ED course:
Triage SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours.
Placed on cardiac monitor, foley deferred, strict I/O started.
Past medical history:
HFrEF, ischemic cardiomyopathy
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
CKD stage 3, baseline Cr 1.4
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, rate controlled
Prior cholecystectomy
Home medications:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 49-51 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 25 mg PO daily
Apixaban 5 mg PO BID
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly
Allergies: sulfa - rash
Social: lives with daughter, former smoker 20 pack-yr quit 12 yrs ago, no alcohol.
Family hx: mother with CHF, father MI at 70.
ROS: positive for dyspnea, orthopnea, leg swelling, fatigue. Negative for fever, chest pain, abdominal pain.
Physical exam:
Vitals: BP 148/88, HR 104 irregular, T 36.8, respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
SpO2 91% on 4L NC
Gen: elderly appearing female, sitting upright, visibly dyspneic
HEENT: JVP elevated to angle of jaw at 45 deg
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, S3 present, no murmur appreciated over crackles
Lungs: crackles to mid lung fields bilaterally, decreased breath sounds at bases
Abd: soft, mildly distended, no tenderness, liver edge 2 cm below costal margin
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally, warm
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit
Labs:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
WBC 8.2, Hgb 11.4, Plt 212
Trop T 0.03 flat on repeat
Imaging:
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
ECG: atrial fibrillation at 104, no acute ST changes, old LBBB-like conduction delay unchanged
Assessment/Plan:
62 yo F with acute decompensated HFrEF, volume overloaded despite outpatient diuretic uptitration.
1. CHF exacerbation - continue IV loop diuresis, strict I/O, daily standing weights, 2g Na diet, 1.5L fluid restriction.
2. Hypoxemia - maintain O2 sat >92%, wean NC as congestion improves.
3. AFib - continue carvedilol and apixaban, monitor rate on telemetry.
4. CKD - daily BMP, watch for rise in Cr with diuresis; hold metformin.
5. Hold sacubitril-valsartan tonight pending renal trend.
Admit to telemetry. Cardiology consulted.
Discussed with daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:15
Subjective: Pt reports mild improvement in breathing but still dyspneic with minimal exertion. Slept sitting up.
Overnight UOP disappointing per RN.
Vitals: T 36.6, BP 132/78, HR 96, RR 24
Remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
I/O last 24h: in 820 mL, out 470 mL
Weight 84.2 kg, down 0.3 kg from admission
Exam:
Gen: less accessory muscle use than admission but still tachypneic
Neck: JVP 12 cm
Lungs: crackles at bases bilaterally, improved above mid field
Cardiac: irregular, S3 persists
Ext: 3+ edema to thighs unchanged
Labs: Na 134, K 3.8, BUN 40, Cr 1.7
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute decompensated CHF, diuretic resistance. Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
2. Add metolazone 5 mg PO once this morning, recheck K in 6 hours.
3. Replete K to goal >4.0, KCl 40 mEq PO x1.
4. Continue O2 to maintain sats >92%, attempt wean this afternoon if UOP improves.
5. Continue holding sacubitril-valsartan given Cr trend; continue carvedilol.
6. Daily weights, strict I/O, fluid restriction 1.5L.
7. Cardiology following, agrees with infusion strategy.
Time spent 30 min including record review.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD5 08:05
Subjective: Pt feels markedly better. Walked hallway with RN this AM without stopping. Sleeping on 1 pillow.
No orthopnea overnight, no PND.
Vitals: T 36.5, BP 118/70, HR 78, RR 18, SpO2 94% on RA since HD4 09:00
I/O last 24h: in 1100 mL, out 2650 mL
Cumulative net negative 7.4 L since admission
Weight 78.8 kg, down 5.4 kg from admission
Exam:
Gen: comfortable, speaking full sentences
Neck: JVP 7 cm
Lungs: clear except trace crackles right base
Cardiac: irregular, rate controlled, no S3 today
Ext: 1+ edema to ankles only
Labs: Na 137, K 4.2, BUN 34, Cr 1.6, Mg 2.0
Assessment/Plan:
1. CHF exacerbation - near euvolemic. Diuretic infusion stopped HD4 20:00, transitioned to furosemide 60 mg IV q12h; switch to PO 80 mg BID today.
2. Renal function stable, resume sacubitril-valsartan at reduced dose 24-26 mg BID this AM.
3. Continue carvedilol 12.5 mg BID, spironolactone 25 mg daily, apixaban.
4. Off supplemental O2, ambulating without desaturation.
5. Heart failure education with RN - daily weights, Na restriction, when to call.
6. Anticipate discharge tomorrow if weight and renal function stable.
7. Repeat echo ordered as outpatient.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - CHF Exacerbation
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted HD1, discharged HD6 at 14:20
Discharge diagnosis: Acute on chronic decompensated systolic heart failure
Secondary: HFrEF EF 30%, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, CKD stage 3, T2DM, hypertension
Brief hospital course:
62 yo F presented with 5 days of progressive dyspnea and leg swelling.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
At presentation: respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Metolazone added HD2 with good diuretic response. Infusion discontinued HD4, transitioned to IV bolus then PO on HD5.
Oxygen weaned to room air HD4 09:00. Ambulated hallway without desaturation HD5 and HD6.
Net negative 8.1 L over stay; discharge weight 78.2 kg, down 6.0 kg from admission.
Sacubitril-valsartan held early for Cr rise to 1.7, resumed HD5 at 24-26 mg BID. Discharge Cr 1.5.
Potassium and magnesium repleted as needed; final K 4.3.
Telemetry: atrial fibrillation, rate controlled, no sustained arrhythmia.
Discharge exam: BP 114/68, HR 74, RR 17, SpO2 95% RA, JVP 6 cm, lungs clear, trace ankle edema.
Discharge medications:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 24-26 mg PO BID
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 25 mg PO daily
Apixaban 5 mg PO BID
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID, resumed at discharge
Instructions:
Weigh daily each morning; call if gain 2 kg in 3 days or 1.5 kg overnight.
Sodium under 2 g daily, fluid under 1.5 L daily.
Return for worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, chest pain, or lightheadedness.
Follow up cardiology in 5 to 7 days with BMP; repeat echo as outpatient.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulatory. Discharged home with daughter.
